html:
The Saur Revolution was a military coup in Kabul on 27 and 28 April 1978 (Saur is the Afghan month). Officers loyal to the communist People's Democratic Party attacked the presidential palace and killed President Mohammed Daoud Khan and much of his family.

The party, the PDPA, took power under Nur Muhammad Taraki, with Hafizullah Amin as his deputy. It renamed the country the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan and moved fast: land redistribution, cancelled peasant debts, limits on bride price, and literacy classes for girls as well as boys.

Few villagers had been asked. Landlords, mullahs and tribal leaders saw an attack on property and religion, and the decrees were enforced by arrests and killings. Revolt spread through the countryside, with its first big flash at the Herat uprising in 1979. The party was also split between its Khalq and Parcham wings, and Amin's faction purged its rivals.

The coup set off the chain that led to the Soviet invasion in December 1979 and the rise of the mujahideen.
